title: Jimmy Noone on the first records and the club called The Nest
summary: They discuss the March 1926 session with St. Cyr and Jimmy Noone, whether they worked together, and where The Nest stood on 35th Street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yes you said that you recorded with Johnny Sincera and they give the date here of March 1926. And then with Jimmy Noon clarinet added a little while later.
Oh yes. He played the clarinet. See.
Was Jimmy working with Johnny or just happened to pick him up to?
I don't think they were working steadily together because Johnny was with an orchestra that played out at the stadium for a long time.

And I don't think he worked with Johnny out there because around that time I think maybe Jimmy Noon was working at a place on 35th Street that they called, a nightclub called The Nest I think at that time. See.
That was close to all the other clubs there wasn't it? Between Entertainers and Sunset Summer and that. Was The Nest on the corner do you have to remember?
No it wasn't on the corner it was near the corner of, it was on the north side of 35th Street. Between I think near the corner of Giles I think it was. Between Giles and Prairie I think. I think.
Well now is that the club that became the Apex? I think.
I don't remember them changing the name to the Apex there.

Across the street, second floor across the street from Sunset. They may have. Well. Was a place called the Apex. They may have. But I'm a little uncertain about the location of the bookstore on the Nest. Uh huh. And Apex I'm pretty sure about but I wondered if it might have been the same.
Well it could have been you know because I'm kind of forgetful so it could have been.
